chunks: And it was narrated from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who had a slave-girl with whom he had intimate relations, and she used to go out for his needs. Then she became pregnant, and he feared that the pregnancy might not be from him. What should he do? Should he sell the slave-girl and the child?
So he said: He may sell the slave-girl, but he must not sell the child, and he does not make him inherit anything from his wealth.

key_terms.الْحَمْلُ: the pregnancy or fetus in this legal context
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: the child born from the pregnancy
key_terms.لَا يَبِيعُ الْوَلَدَ: the child is not to be sold
key_terms.لَا يُوَرِّثُهُ: he does not assign the child inheritance
key_terms.يَبِيعُ الْجَارِيَةَ: selling the slave-girl is deemed permissible here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave-girl becomes pregnant and the master doubts the child is his?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a slave-girl who becomes pregnant when the master doubts that the child is his. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the slave-girl may be sold, but the child may not be sold and is not to inherit from the man’s estate. The narration concerns lineage uncertainty, ownership limits, and inheritance law.
